name: Four Seasons Hotel Istanbul, Bosphorus
positioning: 19th-century Ottoman palace on the Bosphorus waterfront in Beşiktaş
best_for: Couples wanting a hammam and Bosphorus views
Travelers who want a waterfront base near Dolmabahçe Palace and Nişantaşı
Families wanting an Istanbul hotel with a heated outdoor pool

facts.text: The hotel is a 19th-century Ottoman palace transformed into an urban resort, at Çırağan Cad. No. 28 in Beşiktaş, on the Bosphorus.
It sits in Beşiktaş, mere steps from the shopping street of Nişantaşı and Dolmabahçe Palace.
Rooms and suites include the Palace Roof Suite on the top floor of the historic palace building, with a private rooftop terrace, and the Atik Pasha Suite with one to three bedrooms.
Dining includes Yalı (all-day lounge beside the Bosphorus, known for Turkish pide), Aqua (Mediterranean seafood with a Turkish influence), a Sunday brunch, and 24-hour in-room dining.
The spa has 10 treatment rooms and more than 16 treatments, and its hammams are crafted from Marmara marble with an eight-edged star motif.
The hotel has three hammams (traditional Turkish baths), an indoor pool with underwater speakers and a heated outdoor pool by the Bosphorus.
Complimentary services include premium Wi-Fi, a multilingual concierge and a bus shuttle between the two Four Seasons hotels in Istanbul. A boat shuttle between the two hotels is also available.
Istanbul Airport is 43.3 km (26 miles) away, about 47 minutes by car. Sabiha Gökçen Airport is about 40 km (25 miles), 45 to 60 minutes by car.

highlights.text: The Palace Roof Suites are on the top floor of the historic palace building and have a private rooftop terrace.

The spa's hammams are crafted from Marmara marble, with an eight-edged star motif symbolising the eight gates to heaven in the Seljuk Empire, and traditional Turkish hammam journeys for two are offered.
Yalı is an all-day lounge just off the lobby beside the Bosphorus, known for its Turkish pide.
The heated outdoor pool by the Bosphorus is described as family-friendly, and there is also an indoor pool under skylights.

considerations.text: Not every room faces the Bosphorus: Superior Rooms look onto the garden, the street or the historic school building next door, and Four Seasons Rooms offer only glimpses of the Bosphorus or the garden.
The hotel is 43.3 km from Istanbul Airport (about 47 minutes by car) and about 40 km from Sabiha Gökçen (45 to 60 minutes).
WhataHotel lists premium luxury pricing as a trade-off.
Ocakbaşı, the kebab and meze restaurant on the terrace, is described as a pop-up, so it may not always be running.

perks.text: With the WhataHotel Preferred Rate, breakfast for two is free daily (the standard published rate is room only, with breakfast usually extra).
With the WhataHotel Preferred Rate, guests get a priority upgrade if available at check-in.
With the WhataHotel Preferred Rate, guests get a $100 hotel credit.
WhataHotel special offers are combinable with the exclusive perks.
With the WhataHotel Preferred Rate, guests get free Wi-Fi access (the standard published rate charges extra for internet access).
